title: Personne, rien, aucun et seulement
summary: Say nobody, nothing, neither and only without adding an unwanted pas or changing scope.
objectives: Place personne and rien as subjects and objects.
Use aucun(e) and ni ... ni with the right noun pattern.
Restrict one part of a statement with ne ... que.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Negative words replace the missing person or thing
paragraphs: Personne means nobody and rien means nothing in these negative constructions. As objects in a simple tense, they follow the verb: je ne vois personne, je ne comprends rien. As subjects, put them first and retain ne: personne ne vient, rien ne change. Do not add pas to these ordinary patterns.

In the passé composé, rien usually follows the auxiliary before the participle: je n'ai rien vu. Personne normally follows the participle: je n'ai vu personne. A preposition belonging to the verb remains: je ne parle à personne. The noun une personne still means a person; it is not inherently negative.
points: A short answer can be Personne or Rien without a verb. The full careful written sentence includes ne.

examples.note: Rien is the subject; n' precedes the auxiliary.

examples.english: We did not speak to anyone.
examples.note: Personne follows the participle and keeps à.

mistakes.why: For the ordinary intended meaning 'I see nobody', personne replaces pas; marked double negatives can change the meaning.

sections.title: Absence, two exclusions, or a restriction
paragraphs: Aucun/aucune before a noun means no/not a single. Use masculine aucun or feminine aucune, normally with a singular noun and verb where it is the subject. Nouns used only or mainly in the plural can exceptionally have aucuns/aucunes; the tasks here use ordinary count nouns.

Ne ... ni ... ni excludes two alternatives. Unspecified noun quantities can omit articles: ni café ni thé. Keep definite articles when they belong to the meaning or verb: je n'aime ni le café ni le thé. With a negative subject group, ni Paul ni Léa ne viennent is an ordinary plural choice.

Ne ... que means only, not not. Put que immediately before what is restricted: je ne travaille que le lundi restricts the day; je ne fais que travailler restricts the activity. Do not add pas unless you intend 'not only'.
points: Que becomes qu' before a vowel: je n'ai qu'une clé. Ne ... que preserves the positive quantity article; it does not trigger the negative de rule.

examples.note: Aucune agrees with singular feminine question.

examples.french: Nous **ne buvons ni café ni thé**.
examples.english: We drink neither coffee nor tea.
examples.note: Unspecified quantities lose their partitive articles.

examples.french: Je **n'aime ni le café ni le thé**.
examples.english: I like neither coffee nor tea.

examples.note: Que restricts the day, not whether she works.

mistakes.why: Aucun directly introduces this noun; no de is added.

practice.prompt: Use personne as the subject: ___ ne vient.
Replace quelque chose with rien and make negative: J'ai compris quelque chose.
practice.explanation: Rien comes between auxiliary and participle.

practice.prompt: Supply aucun in the correct form: Il n'y a ___ erreur.

choices: I do not have a ticket.
practice.explanation: Ne ... que restricts rather than negates.

practice.prompt: Rewrite using personne as object: Je vois quelqu'un.
Rewrite using personne: Elle a rencontré quelqu'un.
Make Rien the subject of changer in the present; write 'Nothing changes' with ne.
practice.explanation: Rien precedes ne and the singular verb.

practice.prompt: Replace à quelqu'un with à personne: Je téléphone à quelqu'un.
Use aucun with the masculine noun: Nous n'avons ___ problème.
Rewrite with ne ... ni ... ni: Je bois du lait ou du jus. Exclude both.
answers: Je ne bois ni lait ni jus.
practice.explanation: Unspecified quantities omit the partitive articles.

practice.prompt: Rewrite with ne ... ni ... ni: J'aime le froid et la pluie. Exclude both.
answers: Je n'aime ni le froid ni la pluie.

practice.prompt: Replace seulement with ne ... que: Je travaille seulement le soir.
answers: Je ne travaille que le soir.
practice.explanation: Que immediately precedes the restricted time.

practice.prompt: Use rien: Nous avons acheté quelque chose. Make the sentence negative.
Supply aucun in the correct form as subject determiner: ___ place n'est libre.
Replace seulement with ne ... que: Elle a seulement une sœur.
practice.explanation: Que elides; une remains because the meaning is positive restriction.

practice.prompt: Je ne fais que travailler restricts:
choices: The activity: working is all I do.
The day on which I work.
answers: The activity: working is all I do.
practice.explanation: Que immediately precedes the restricted activity.

production_task.prompt: Explain why a room booking will not work and propose one limited alternative. Use no one, no available item and only.
production_task.model_answer: Personne ne peut ouvrir la salle samedi. Aucune autre salle n'est libre ce jour-là. Nous ne pouvons organiser la rencontre que dimanche. Je n'ai rien réservé pour le moment.
production_task.translation: Nobody can open the room on Saturday. No other room is available that day. We can organise the meeting only on Sunday. I have not booked anything for now.
rubric: Do not add pas to ordinary personne/rien/aucun patterns.
Use que before the actual restriction.
